stem: The region around a magnet where its magnetic force can be detected is called the __________.
solution: The magnetic field is the region around a magnet where its force acts.

stem: The lines used to represent a magnetic field are called __________.
solution: Magnetic field lines represent the direction and strength of the magnetic field.

stem: Magnetic field lines outside a magnet run from the __________ pole to the __________ pole.
solution: Outside a magnet, field lines emerge from the north pole and enter the south pole.

stem: The scientist who discovered that an electric current produces a magnetic effect is __________.
solution: Oersted discovered that a current-carrying wire deflects a nearby compass needle, revealing the magnetic effect of current.

stem: A compass needle near a current-carrying wire __________.
solution: The compass needle deflects because the current produces a magnetic field around the wire.

stem: The pattern of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire consists of __________.
solution: The magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor consists of concentric circles.

stem: The rule used to find the direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying wire is the __________.
solution: The right-hand thumb rule gives the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying wire.

stem: A coil of many circular turns of wire is called a __________.
solution: A solenoid is a coil of many circular turns; it produces a magnetic field like a bar magnet.

stem: A current-carrying solenoid behaves like a __________.
solution: A current-carrying solenoid produces a magnetic field similar to that of a bar magnet.

stem: A coil of wire wound around a soft iron core, magnetic only when current flows, is an __________.
solution: An electromagnet is a solenoid with a soft-iron core, magnetic only while current flows.

stem: A current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field experiences a __________.
solution: A current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field experiences a force (the motor effect).

stem: The rule used to find the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is __________.
solution: Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field.

stem: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the thumb points in the direction of the __________.
solution: In Fleming's left-hand rule: thumb → force/motion, forefinger → field, middle finger → current.

stem: A device that converts electrical energy into mechanical energy is an __________.
solution: An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical (rotational) energy.

stem: The electric motor works on the principle that a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences a __________.
solution: A current-carrying coil in a magnetic field experiences a torque that rotates it — the basis of the motor.

stem: The phenomenon of producing an electric current by changing the magnetic field around a conductor is called __________.
solution: Electromagnetic induction is the production of a current by changing the magnetic field near a conductor.

stem: Electromagnetic induction was discovered by __________.
solution: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction.

stem: A device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy is a __________.
solution: An electric generator (dynamo) converts mechanical energy into electrical energy using electromagnetic induction.

stem: The rule used to find the direction of induced current is __________.
solution: Fleming's right-hand rule gives the direction of induced current in a generator.

stem: The type of current that reverses its direction periodically is called __________.
solution: Alternating current (AC) periodically reverses its direction.

stem: The type of current that flows in only one direction is called __________.
solution: Direct current (DC) flows in only one direction, as provided by a cell or battery.

stem: The frequency of AC supplied in India is __________.
solution: The AC mains supply in India has a frequency of 50 Hz.

stem: An advantage of AC over DC is that AC can be __________ over long distances.
solution: AC can be transmitted over long distances with less energy loss, using transformers.

stem: The strength of an electromagnet can be increased by __________.
options: increasing the number of turns and the current
solution: More turns of wire and a larger current make the electromagnet stronger.

stem: Electromagnets are used in devices like __________.
solution: Electromagnets are used in electric bells, cranes, loudspeakers, motors and many machines.

stem: The three wires in a domestic circuit are live, neutral and __________.
solution: Domestic wiring has live (red/brown), neutral (black/blue) and earth (green) wires.

stem: The earth wire is a safety measure that connects the metal case of an appliance to the __________.
solution: The earth wire connects the appliance's metal case to the ground, safely carrying leakage current away.

stem: An overload or short circuit produces a large current that is cut off by a __________.
solution: A fuse or MCB breaks the circuit during overload or short circuit, preventing damage and fire.

stem: The magnetic field inside a long current-carrying solenoid is __________.
options: uniform and strong (like a bar magnet)
solution: Inside a long solenoid, the magnetic field is uniform and strong, similar to that of a bar magnet.

stem: A soft iron core is used in an electromagnet because it __________.
solution: Soft iron magnetises strongly when current flows and loses magnetism quickly when it stops.

stem: The force on a current-carrying conductor is greatest when the conductor is __________ to the magnetic field.
solution: The force is maximum when the current-carrying conductor is perpendicular to the magnetic field.

stem: The commutator in a DC motor is used to __________.
options: reverse the direction of current in the coil to keep it rotating in one direction
solution: The commutator (split ring) reverses the current in the coil every half turn, keeping the motor rotating in one direction.

stem: A galvanometer is a device used to detect the presence of __________ in a circuit.
solution: A galvanometer detects and indicates the presence and direction of a small electric current.

stem: The induced current in a coil is larger when the magnet is moved __________.
options: faster (rate of change of field is greater)
solution: A faster change in the magnetic field induces a larger current (Faraday's law).

stem: Which of the following converts electrical energy into mechanical energy?
solution: An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical energy; a generator does the reverse.

stem: Which of the following converts mechanical energy into electrical energy?
solution: A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by electromagnetic induction.

stem: The magnetic field of a current-carrying circular loop is strongest at __________.
solution: The magnetic field of a circular current loop is strongest and most uniform at its centre.

stem: Electric short circuits and overloading can be avoided by using a fuse of __________.
solution: A fuse of a proper (safe) current rating melts before dangerous overload, protecting the circuit.

stem: In an electric generator, the coil is rotated in a magnetic field to __________.
solution: Rotating the coil in a magnetic field changes the field through it, inducing an electric current.

stem: The direction of the magnetic field around a wire reverses when the __________ is reversed.
solution: Reversing the direction of the current reverses the direction of its magnetic field.

stem: Loudspeakers use the __________ to convert electrical signals into sound.
solution: In loudspeakers, a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field vibrates a diaphragm, producing sound (motor effect).

stem: The strength of the magnetic field due to a current-carrying wire increases with __________.
solution: A larger current produces a stronger magnetic field around the wire.

stem: The magnetic field produced by a bar magnet and by a solenoid are __________.
solution: A current-carrying solenoid produces a magnetic field pattern very similar to that of a bar magnet.

stem: The purpose of an electric fuse in the live wire is to __________.
options: break the circuit if the current exceeds a safe value
solution: The fuse in the live wire melts and breaks the circuit during overload or short circuit, ensuring safety.

stem: Electromagnetic induction is used in the working of __________.
solution: Generators and transformers work on the principle of electromagnetic induction.

stem: Two magnetic field lines can never __________.
solution: Field lines never cross because the field can have only one direction at any point.

stem: The closeness of magnetic field lines indicates a __________ magnetic field.
solution: Closely spaced field lines indicate a stronger magnetic field; widely spaced lines a weaker field.

stem: The magnetic effect of electric current was discovered by __________.
solution: Hans Christian Oersted discovered that a current produces a magnetic field.

stem: An electric motor converts electrical energy into __________ energy.
solution: An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical (rotational) energy.

stem: The production of a current by a changing magnetic field is called __________.
solution: Electromagnetic induction produces a current when the magnetic field near a conductor changes.

stem: The overall message of the chapter 'Magnetic Effects of Electric Current' is that:
options: an electric current produces a magnetic field, a current-carrying conductor in a field experiences a force (used in motors), and a changing field induces a current (used in generators)
motors and generators do not exist
solution: The chapter links electricity and magnetism: magnetic effect of current, force on conductors (motor), electromagnetic induction (generator), and domestic electric circuits and safety.

stem: A magnet has two poles: north and __________.
solution: Every magnet has a north pole and a south pole.

stem: The direction of the magnetic field at a point is taken as the direction in which the __________ pole of a compass points.
solution: The field direction is defined by the direction the north pole of a compass needle points.

stem: Magnetic field lines emerge from the __________ pole and merge into the south pole outside a magnet.
solution: Field lines run from north to south outside the magnet.

stem: Two magnetic field lines can __________.
solution: Field lines never intersect, because the field has only one direction at each point.

stem: A current-carrying conductor produces a __________ around it.
solution: A magnetic field is produced around a wire carrying an electric current.

stem: The rule used to find the direction of the magnetic field around a straight current-carrying conductor is the __________ rule.
solution: The right-hand thumb rule gives the direction of the magnetic field around a wire.

stem: The magnetic field due to a current-carrying wire is stronger when the current is __________.
solution: A larger current produces a stronger magnetic field.

stem: A coil of many turns of insulated wire is called a __________.
solution: A solenoid is a coil of many turns; it behaves like a bar magnet when current flows.

stem: The magnetic field inside a current-carrying solenoid is __________.
solution: Inside a solenoid the field is uniform and strong, like that of a bar magnet.

stem: A soft iron core inside a current-carrying solenoid makes a strong __________.
solution: A solenoid with a soft iron core forms a strong electromagnet.

stem: The rule to find the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is __________.
solution: Fleming's left-hand rule gives the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor.

stem: The force on a current-carrying conductor is maximum when it is placed __________ to the magnetic field.
solution: The force is maximum when the conductor is perpendicular to the field.

stem: A device that converts electrical energy into mechanical energy is an electric __________.
solution: An electric motor converts electrical energy into mechanical (rotational) energy.

stem: The production of an induced current by a changing magnetic field is called electromagnetic __________.
solution: Electromagnetic induction is the generation of current by a changing magnetic field.

stem: The phenomenon of electromagnetic induction was discovered by __________.
solution: Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction.

stem: The rule to find the direction of induced current is __________.
solution: Fleming's right-hand rule gives the direction of induced current.

stem: A device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy is an electric __________.
solution: An electric generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by induction.

stem: The current that reverses its direction periodically is called __________ current.
solution: Alternating current (AC) reverses direction periodically.

stem: The current that flows in one direction only is called __________ current.
solution: Direct current (DC), such as from a cell, flows in only one direction.

stem: In India, the frequency of the domestic AC supply is __________.
solution: The domestic AC supply in India has a frequency of 50 Hz.

stem: In a domestic circuit, the wire kept at a high potential is the __________ wire.
solution: The live wire (usually red) carries current at high potential.

stem: The earth wire in domestic wiring is used as a __________ measure.
solution: The earth wire provides a safe path for leakage current, preventing shocks.

stem: A short circuit occurs when the live and neutral wires __________.
options: touch directly, causing a sudden large current
solution: A short circuit is a direct contact of live and neutral wires, causing a large current.

stem: Overloading of an electric circuit occurs when __________.
options: too many appliances draw excessive current
solution: Overloading happens when too many appliances draw more current than the wiring can handle.

stem: The magnetic field around a bar magnet is strongest at its __________.
solution: The field is strongest near the poles, where the field lines are closest together.

stem: Closely spaced magnetic field lines indicate a __________ magnetic field.
solution: The closer the field lines, the stronger the magnetic field.

stem: In an electric motor, the device that reverses the current direction in the coil each half rotation is the __________.
solution: The split-ring commutator reverses the current in the coil to keep the motor rotating.

stem: The strength of an electromagnet can be increased by increasing the number of __________ in the coil.
solution: More turns of wire (and more current) increase the strength of an electromagnet.

stem: Fleming's left-hand rule is used for a __________, while the right-hand rule is used for a generator.
solution: Fleming's left-hand rule applies to the motor (force); right-hand rule applies to the generator (induced current).

stem: A magnetic compass placed near a current-carrying wire shows deflection, demonstrating the __________ effect of current.
solution: The deflection of a compass near a wire shows the magnetic effect of current (Oersted's experiment).
